original_test_intent: Verify that the product FRU reports the approved finished-system product name and that the authoritative BMC UI/OEM inventory presents the same product identity.
original_method: Bind the product FRU and UI/API resource to the same system, retrieve raw product-name values securely, map only approved customer/OEM/localized aliases and revision suffixes, and compare with the versioned product specification.
manual_activity: Supply the authoritative finished-product name, validated FRU/UI field mapping and approved customer/OEM/localization/revision aliases; no physical action is required.
required_inputs: Approved customer, OEM and localized aliases
safety_requirements: Use read-only FRU and API operations
Never write FRU or issue raw mutation/PATCH/product control
Do not treat a generic resource `Name` as FRU Product Name without mapping
Apply only approved aliases and localization
Stop on multiple product records or model ambiguity
agent_execution_scope: Bind the intended product FRU record
Resolve the validated OEM/UI product-name source
Capture complete redacted evidence and statuses

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `ipmitool fru print` can expose Product Name, but `/Chassis/system` and `.Product.Name` are unvalidated. In Redfish-like APIs a resource Name can be descriptive rather than the FRU product identity, so a raw match or missing-path fallback is not sufficient.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use secure read-only access to capture the bound product FRU and validated OEM/UI product-name/model property, retain raw strings, apply the approved alias/localization/revision mapping and compare with the authoritative product specification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The `ipmitool fru list` inspection, Product Name field, UI agreement criterion and 2/0-minute timing are preserved; resource, property, aliases and expected name are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a product-scoped comparator that records FRU/API resource identity, raw names, language/alias/revision tokens, policy version and canonical product result.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces an assumed generic Name property and visual review with a product-specific semantic mapping and authoritative oracle.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects wrong system naming, customer branding and model/revision mismatches while preserving the intended read-only cross-source check.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A permissive alias table can hide the wrong product family; localized display names may be valid but must be traceable to the approved base identity.

project_override_considerations: Product Name is system/product scope, distinct from Board Product. The private scripts may contain mapping rules but are unavailable and must not be inferred.
expected_evidence: Complete redacted FRU output and status
Resolved OEM/UI product resource and property with response status
Raw FRU and UI product-name strings
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master and prior reviews consistently target Product Name. The unvalidated path and missing product oracle/mapping are execution gaps rather than a conflicting source purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The finished-product naming check is clear. The authoritative name, field mapping and alias policy are finite project packages.

review_improvement: Prevents a generic API display name, board model or unapproved customer alias from being accepted as the finished product's FRU Product Name.
independent_technical_reasoning: A product-level FRU name may be an engineering model, customer SKU name or localized brand, while an API resource's generic `Name` can merely label that resource. The test needs a declared semantic mapping and authoritative product oracle before comparing strings. Board Product is a different component-level field and cannot fill that role. With those project inputs the operation is fully read-only; until then the correct classification is REQUIRES.
